implementationPlan.note:
THE BUDGET_REF SLOT (DoD-5) — filled, drilled, and split as the step sanctioned.

RED FIRST, both arms, in approval-record-facts.test.ts: `Tests 2 failed | 21 passed (23)`. Arm 1 failed because `derived.budgetRef` was undefined; arm 2 failed with `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { …(2) }` because no upstream was carried.

WHAT THE ARMS ASSERT. (1) "derives a budget ref the activation bind-back itself accepts" — over the production-seeded `reviewableStore()` (driveThrough "approval.decide"), it takes the derived ref and asks the PRODUCTION `verifyBudgetCommitment` — the same fence that guards activation — whether it accepts it. That is the strong form the DoD asks for: not "equals a digest this test recomputed", which any shared bug would satisfy, but the seam and the fence agreeing through production on both sides. It then additionally pins the ref to `budgetCommitmentDigest(budgetCommitmentMaterial(...))` so the notion is the commitment specifically. (2) "leaves the slot ABSENT and carries the upstream when nothing durable answers" — over a bare store the key is not present at all (`"budgetRef" in result.derived` is false, so `{}` and a zero digest stay different answers) and `upstream` is exactly `{ code: "BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING", layer: "DAEMON_PREREQUISITE" }`, the ledger reader's own code and layer.

WHY THE ARMS GRADE `derived` AND NOT THE OK PATH. The roster order is RISK_TIER, STEP_UP, POLICY_REF, BUDGET_REF (approval-intent.ts:68-77) and RISK_TIER still has no producer — task-f42d5165 owns it — so the walk always stops there and BUDGET_REF is unreachable as `missing`. `ApprovalRecordFactsIncomplete.derived` exists precisely so derivation is gradable behind a refusal, which is what these arms use. Filling the slot is still real: FACT_ESTABLISHED's BUDGET_REF predicate now answers true.

GREEN. `deriveApprovalBudgetRef` composes the run's OWN durable identity: `readApprovalIntentSources(store, projectId, runId)` supplies the verified ApprovedRunBinding, graphRevisionRef and goalRef, so a genuine `GenesisApprovedRun` is built from durable state with nothing fabricated and nothing presented by a caller (the request vocabulary is {projectId, runId}). It then composes the SHARED builder — `budgetCommitmentMaterial` + `budgetCommitmentDigest` — never a second material list. Refusals forward the code and layer of whoever said no: the ledger reader, the run binding, or the material builder.

ONE UPSTREAM SLOT, filled in ROSTER ORDER: the policy ref is listed before the budget ref, so its refusal wins when it has one; the budget upstream fills in otherwise. That is not a downgrade — the policy path can refuse with no upstream at all (which is why arm 2 saw `undefined` before this change), and a precise builder code beats nothing. The rule is stated in the code, not left to inference.

I also corrected the slot's own doc comment, which asserted the ref could NEVER be set here because it is minted at activation. That stopped being true with task-61a2e8ad: the commitment covers material durable at decide time. Leaving the old prose would have left the next reader believing the slot is unfillable.

The edit took approval-record-facts.ts to 253 lines, past the 250 cap. `deriveApprovalBudgetRef` and its result type moved to a new sibling apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-budget-ref.ts (55 lines) with the exact one-line LF bridge approval-budget-ref.js — the same split task-3b61860f took for the third slot into approval-policy-ref.ts. approval-record-facts.ts is back to 213 lines.
